sources.title: Millet noodles in Late Neolithic China — Nature

notes: 喇家面条的原料一度定为粟，后有实验质疑纯粟面团能否拉出该形态；遗址人骨同位素仍以粟为主。条目以考古年代为主，不单独标争议。
notes_en: Lajia noodles were initially identified as millet; later experiments questioned whether pure millet dough could be stretched into that form. Isotopic evidence from human bones at the site still indicates a predominantly millet-based diet. This entry uses the archaeological date without a separate dispute flag.
summary_zh: 青海喇家遗址出土约公元前2000年的面条遗存，是目前已知最早的实物；后世小麦面条在宋以后更为普及。
summary_en: Noodles preserved at Lajia in Qinghai, about 2000 BCE, are the earliest known physical remains. Wheat noodles became everyday fare in China especially from the Song onward.
summary_ja: 青海省の喇家で保存された紀元前2000年頃の麺が、知られている最古の実物である。小麦の麺はとくに宋以降、中国の日常食になった。
